correctness.rationale: The central finite-observation simulation is proved by induction on modal depth: for each nonderivable box operand \(\chi\), any hypothetical K theorem \((\bigwedge B^+)\to\chi\) would belong to \(L_{n-1}\) by the induction hypothesis, contradicting \(\Gamma\not\vdash_{L_{n-1}}\chi\). Ordinary K completeness gives a child model, and finite-model property plus bounded unraveling gives a finite tree without changing relevant formulas. Assembling witnesses matches every box operand, hence all requested formulas. The reverse Kripke-to-derivability interpretation uses the successor theory and soundness of \(L_n\subseteq\mathsf K\). Empty-assumption interpretations and induction on boxed tautologies certify the sharp omitted depth at all natural stages. No computation substitutes for the unbounded proof.

value.rationale: The natural object is the finite approximant chain to the least fixed point of a recently studied modal derivability operator. The theorem does not merely restate K completeness: it constructs a finite Kripke root for arbitrary evaluation-logic interpretations and any finite set of observations, proves a uniform exact logical-depth cutoff at every stage, exhibits the first missing formula, and settles the exact stabilization ordinal \(\omega\). These are structural and sharp invariants of the full unbounded chain, not arbitrary low-cardinality checks.
